summary:
Has NASA tested fire in air like the air in a future Moon base?

WHAT WE BUILT
Finkers: a public website that brings together 24 NASA combustion investigations (738 tests with oxygen and pressure) so users can:
- Compare cabin conditions: pick a habitat or enter their own oxygen, pressure and gravity.
- Find relevant experiments that were run in similar air.
- Open the original NASA measurement behind any result, down to the file and row.
- Ask questions in plain English: an AI answers only from the matching NASA records and cites each one.

WHAT WE FOUND
- Station reference (21% O2, 1 atm): 179 close matches.
- Illustrative Moon Base preset (34% O2, 0.57 atm): 0 close matches and 37 in a wider range.
- "Close" means within ±2 oxygen points and ±0.05 atm. The comparison uses oxygen and pressure only.

WHY IT MATTERS
Planned lunar cabins use more oxygen than today's spacecraft, and more oxygen makes materials burn more easily. Finkers gives researchers a starting point for choosing which studies to read and where further testing could help.
details:
THE PROBLEM

NASA has spent decades studying how fire behaves in low gravity. A researcher asking what applies to a particular cabin may need to work through several investigations, each with its own test conditions, units, and way of reporting results. We built Finkers around that first research question: has NASA tested fire in air like the air in this cabin?

WHAT IT DOES

Finkers brings together 24 combustion investigations from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) archive: 1,711 test records, 738 of which report both oxygen and pressure.

- Compare a cabin: select a habitat or enter your own oxygen concentration and pressure. Finkers shows where NASA's evidence is close, where it is wider, and where it is missing.

- Explore experiments: filter by fuel, investigation, and reported outcome.

- Open the source: selecting a point or row opens the original measurement, including its PSI accession, filename, and CSV row.

- Share the result: download a cabin evidence brief with the counts, matching rules, and source links.

- Ask a question: type a question in plain English. Asking which FLEX tests report methanol extinction returns 126 matching rows in our snapshot, and users can open each cited record to see what NASA actually measured.

WHAT WE FOUND

The station reference (21% oxygen, 1 atmosphere) has 179 close matches. Our illustrative Moon Base preset (34% oxygen, 0.57 atmospheres) has zero, with 37 more in a wider range. The close window is within two oxygen percentage points and 0.05 atmospheres of the selected cabin. The zero applies to that window and the data in our snapshot. Fuel, geometry, ventilation, and gravity still matter when deciding how a particular result applies.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

Most tools start from a list of experiments. Finkers starts from the cabin a crew will live in, and shows what NASA has not tested as clearly as what it has. Every number and every AI answer links back to the original NASA row, so results can be checked, not just trusted.

TOOLS

React and JavaScript for the interface, Python and Node.js for data preparation, GroqCloud (openai/gpt-oss-20b) for answering questions, deployed on Vercel.

IMPACT

We hope Finkers helps students and researchers find relevant evidence sooner and identify which questions, such as materials and airflow in oxygen-rich, low-pressure cabins, need a closer look.

Live project: https://flame-in-freefall-beta.vercel.app

Source code: https://github.com/nithinram123/finkers-flame-in-freefall
